name: Memory Shard
description: Auto-compresses history into a compact, resumable memory shard once the chat reaches ~30k tokens, feeds the latest shard back into context, and can hide the story it has absorbed
author: Neconyan
prompt:
Goal: Summarise roleplay history into a clear, human-readable memory shard that restores full story continuity if older chat history is hidden or lost. Write in plain English Markdown so a reader can scan and edit any line without learning codes or symbols.

# Task Type
- Consolidation: every input block is already a `# MEMORY SHARD: [ID]-[NUM]`. Merge them into one master shard headed `# CONSOLIDATED MEMORY SHARD: [ID]-MASTER`.
- Compression: raw chat messages or unsharded scenes are present. Write a new shard headed `# MEMORY SHARD: [ID]-[NEXT NUM]` covering the new material and leave earlier shards intact.

# Reading Order
1. Read the full input before writing.
2. Spot the emotional turning points and permanent changes first.
3. Trace causes and consequences clearly from those turning points.
4. Keep high-impact moments detailed; condense or leave out trivial filler that can be inferred.

# Priority Weights
Tag every story event with one weight in brackets. Any explicit intimate scene is `[Critical]`.
- `[Minor]` - Atmosphere, brief movement, or small exchanges worth noting briefly.
- `[Moderate]` - Advances the plot, reveals useful information, or shifts a mood.
- `[Major]` - High emotional impact, a turning point, or a key dialogue moment.
- `[Critical]` - Permanently alters a character, relationship, world fact, or continuity; includes intimate scenes.
Leave out trivial filler unless a callback or payoff relies on it.

# Sections
Start directly with the `# ` shard heading, followed by `## ` sections in this order. Omit a section only if nothing in the input belongs there (for example, omit `## Intimate Moments` when no explicit intimate scene happened). Use plain labelled bullets rather than pipe-delimited rows or shorthand codes.

## Current Snapshot
Place the immediate state of play first so anyone can verify or edit it at a glance:
- Location: Current setting and immediate surroundings
- Time: Time of day, weather, or elapsed time
- Present: Characters currently in the scene
- Situation: What is happening right now
- Mood: Emotional atmosphere in the room
- Physical: Injuries, exhaustion, clothing, or held items that matter right now
- Next up: Immediate unresolved action, question, or tension

## Tone & Atmosphere
Write 1 to 2 plain sentences describing the genre, pacing, emotional tone, and prose style of the story.

## Characters
Give each active or newly introduced character a `### Name` subheading with flat labelled bullets (keep only the lines that apply):
### Character Name
- Role: Protagonist, ally, rival, or current role in the story
- Appearance: Notable build, scars, clothing, or visual traits
- Personality: Core traits and current demeanour
- Abilities: Skills, magic, gear, or limits
- Status: Alive, injured, captive, whereabouts, and current emotional state
- Growth: Meaningful changes, realisations, or skills gained in this segment

## Relationships
List meaningful pairings and recent shifts as flat bullets:
- Character A -> Character B (short summary): Current trust, closeness, tension, or shared history in plain words.

## World & Setting
Record enduring world facts, locations, factions, rules, or important items as flat bullets:
- Category: Clear factual note.

## Story Events
List events in chronological order. Give each event a numbered `### ` heading with its weight tag and location in parentheses, followed by flat bullets:
### 1. [Critical] Short Event Title (Location)
- What happened: Cause, action, and immediate outcome in 1 to 2 crisp sentences.
- Aftermath: Lasting consequences, injuries, or shifts caused by this event.
- Emotions & state: How the key characters felt and looked during or after it.

## Key Scenes
Expand `[Major]` and `[Critical]` moments into concise prose (50 to 180 words each) so the texture of the scene survives compression:
### Event Title or Scene Name
Write a vivid, grounded prose paragraph preserving the exact emotional turn, physical detail, and subtext of the scene.

## Memorable Quotes & Voices
Keep verbatim lines that define character voice, promises, confessions, or callbacks:
- Speaker: "Exact quote from the chat" (brief context or delivery tone)

## Sensory Anchors
Note recurring sights, sounds, scents, or textures tied to people or places:
- Anchor detail (Sense): Where it appeared and why it matters.

## Callbacks & Loose Threads
Track foreshadowed details and unresolved plot points with a clear status tag (`[Planted]`, `[Open]`, or `[Resolved]`):
- [Planted] Short title: Detail introduced and where it could pay off.
- [Open] Short title: Unresolved mystery, promise, or threat and who knows about it.
- [Resolved] Short title: How a previously open thread was paid off or closed.

## Intimate Moments
Include this section only when explicit romantic or intimate scenes occurred. Keep adult, consensual scenes only; leave out any non-consensual or underage sexual content.
### Event Title (Participants)
- Details: Act type, pace, emotional dynamic, and aftermath.
- Source prose: Preserve the original intimate prose faithfully without paraphrasing it away.

# Compression Rules
- Every fact comes from the provided chat or earlier shards; leave out guesses or invented details.
- Prefer plain English words over cryptic abbreviations, numeric relationship scores, or pipe tables.
- Keep `## Current Snapshot`, `## Characters`, `## Relationships`, and `## Story Events` complete enough to resume the story smoothly on their own.
- Quote exact dialogue verbatim inside quotation marks.
- When updating from earlier shards, carry forward active facts, open threads, and character changes cleanly.

# Consolidation Rules
When consolidating multiple shards into `# CONSOLIDATED MEMORY SHARD: [ID]-MASTER`:
- Merge duplicate character entries into one up-to-date profile per character, preserving their full arc.
- Renumber `## Story Events` in clean chronological order from `1.` onward across the merged shards.
- Merge `## Relationships` into current states while keeping major turning points noted.
- Update `## Callbacks & Loose Threads` so resolved threads are marked `[Resolved]` and open ones stay `[Open]`.
- Keep `## Current Snapshot` anchored to the latest shard.
- Preserve all `[Critical]` events, `## Key Scenes`, verbatim quotes, and `## Intimate Moments` source prose intact.

# Final Check
Verify before finishing:
- Heading matches `# MEMORY SHARD: [ID]-[NEXT NUM]` or `# CONSOLIDATED MEMORY SHARD: [ID]-MASTER`.
- `## Current Snapshot` matches the exact end of the input.
- Every `[Major]` and `[Critical]` event is accounted for in `## Story Events`, `## Characters`, `## Relationships`, and `## Key Scenes`.
- All formatting is clean, flat, human-editable Markdown with no pipe tables or shorthand keys.

# Mewmory Reference
When Mewmory facts or character views appear below, cross-check names, world facts, promises, and relationships against them so this shard stays consistent with long-term memory. If a section is empty, rely on the chat and previous shards.

<story_memory>
{{mewmory-facts}}
</story_memory>
<character_views>
{{mewmory-interview}}
</character_views>
